subject: Continuity sequencing & KV persistence snapshot request

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@clearshore.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clearshore Security <security@clearshore.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence request: continuity sequencing + KV persistence snapshot

Alex —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As part of our SOC 2 and SIG intake for Redwood, we need a compact set of artifacts that demonstrate your operational sequencing for a warm->hot failover and evidence of KV persistence for RPO validation. Specifically we need:

- A point-in-time KV snapshot (manifest + checksums) showing last successful commit before 2026-11-30 02:00 UTC.
- A short sequenced runbook (bullet steps) for multi-region failover: how traffic is routed, cache warming steps, and the expected handoff order for stateful services.
- Measured RTO/RPO numbers from a recent rehearsal (timestamps + observed failover duration).
- Chain-of-custody steps for snapshots (who executed, where stored, retention).
- A one-paragraph signed attestation we can include in our evidence pack stating Redwood's ability to meet the RTO/RPO bounds in prod for our tier.

Can you deliver these artifacts by EOD PST tomorrow (2026-12-01)? We may request a short live witness (30–45m) to walk through the replay and snapshot validation.

If there's anything not possible or requires escalation, flag it and we can coordinate with procurement/security.

Appreciate it —
Maria Garcia
Senior Risk Manager, Clearshore Financial
maria.garcia@clearshore.com
+1 415 555 0112

---
Attachments requested: KV snapshot manifest; runbook excerpt; RTO/RPO logs (if already available).

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the list and the timeline. We can provide everything you requested by EOD tomorrow. Quick summary of next steps from our side:

1) Attached: runbook-continuity-v2.pdf — condensed sequencing for warm->hot promotion with explicit traffic cutover steps and TTLs for cache rehydration.
2) KV snapshot: we have a validated manifest and checksums from the nightly snapshot run that finished 2026-11-30 01:54:12 UTC. I will request Marissa to attach the manifest and the replay index file.
3) RTO/RPO sample: we ran a rehearsal on 2026-10-28; I will extract the measured timings and include the timeline spreadsheet.
4) Chain-of-custody: Marissa will provide the snapshot owner, signing key id, and S3 path with object version ids.
5) Attestation: I will provide a signed paragraph (Director, Product Operations) that you can drop into your pack.

We can also run a 30-minute live witness next Thu (2026-12-03) 09:00–09:45 PST to walk the replay and validate checksums if that works for your security team. If you prefer earlier, we can try 2026-12-02 16:00 PST.

Action items for internal ops (cc'd): Marissa — please populate the manifest and provide the S3 object versions + small checklist for how the KV snapshot is produced and verified. Jonas — can you include a one-paragraph attestation (signed) and confirm the rehearsal RTO/RPO numbers.

Thanks —

Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the artifacts so far — the manifest and timeline look good. Two quick clarifications before we close this out for SOC 2:

1) Point-in-time recovery: can you confirm whether prefix-level cache metadata (TTL + last-updated token) is preserved by the snapshot and replay process, or whether prefix warming is always a rebuild from origin traffic? We need to document whether our RPO covers metadata vs. payload (we prefer both).

2) Attestation language: we need a one-paragraph statement signed by Redwood that says: "Redwood Inference attests that for Clearshore Financial tier X, the standard warm-standby promotion process demonstrated in our 2026-10-28 rehearsal achieves an RTO of <= 10 minutes and RPO of <= 5 minutes, subject to network boundary conditions summarized in the runbook." If you can provide the signed version (PDF) that would be ideal.

If you can confirm (1) and provide the signed attestation by EOD tomorrow we'll mark this item closed. Appreciate the ops checklist — the chain-of-custody details are suitable.

Regards,
Maria
